html:
The Wajarri are an Aboriginal people of the Mid West of Western Australia, with a large territory around the upper Murchison and Gascoyne rivers. They are one of the Yamatji peoples, and their language is one of the strongest surviving Aboriginal languages of the region.

Their neighbours on the map include the Nhanda and Amangu toward the coast, the Badimaya to the south and the Malgana and Yinggarda to the west. Sheep stations spread through the Murchison from the 1870s.

In recent decades part of Wajarri country, around Boolardy Station, became the site of the Murchison Radio-astronomy Observatory, chosen because the area is so quiet of radio noise. It hosts part of the Square Kilometre Array telescope, and agreements with Wajarri people govern its use of the land. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
